topic: Can MVDR beamforming sufficiently compensate for pattern degradation in array-fed reflectors during element failures?
consensus_response: MVDR beamforming exhibits significant robustness against feed element failures by reducing defocusing and improving spacing, resulting in less gain loss compared to conventional designs. This leads to a reduction in signal degradation caused by element failures.  The effectiveness of MVDR is due to its ability to adjust the signal patterns through beamforming. This provides superior performance even with failed elements, offering significant cost savings in terms of redundancy or margin planning.
